title: Ethics and Consumer Protection
implementation_note: Free ongoing practice design. Repeated attempts support learning only; this artifact does not implement access, enrollment, time tracking, or credit. Original public formative items are separate from any protected final examination.

items.prompt: Two otherwise matched applicants request information about the same eligible loans. Staff give one applicant fewer options solely because she is a woman. Neither has received a credit decision. Which finding is supported?

choices.text: A concern exists only if the narrower explanation later causes a denial.
choices.feedback: Treatment during the information and application process is covered; a final denial is not required for this discrimination concern.

choices.text: The unequal information based on sex raises a Regulation B treatment violation now.
choices.feedback: Correct. The stipulated difference and its prohibited basis concern the current treatment, not merely a possible later outcome.

choices.text: The treatment is acceptable if both ultimately receive the same interest rate.
choices.feedback: Equal final rates do not erase unequal information provided on a prohibited basis.

choices.text: The proper correction is to remove the extra options from the other applicant.
choices.feedback: Withholding information from both is not an appropriate correction for the discriminatory restriction.

items.prompt: An originator tells a prospective applicant, "Because you are retired, applying here will only get you worse terms." No individual repayment facts have been reviewed. Under the current Regulation B discouragement rule, what is the best assessment?

choices.text: It is outside the rule because the consumer has not submitted a signed application.
choices.feedback: The current provision expressly reaches directed statements to prospective applicants as well as applicants.

choices.text: It is permitted because retirement always reduces repayment ability.
choices.feedback: That is a categorical assumption; relevant individual income facts have not been evaluated.

choices.text: It requires the creditor to approve the applicant on the best available terms.
choices.feedback: Correcting discouragement does not guarantee approval or eliminate lawful eligibility and pricing requirements.

choices.text: It conveys worse terms on a prohibited basis rather than an individual credit analysis.
choices.feedback: Correct. The directed statement links expected unfavorable treatment to retirement instead of supported repayment facts.

items.prompt: An applicant relies on a pension. The amount is verified, but a record says one component ends in four months. What should the reviewer do?

choices.text: Evaluate the actual ending component and the remaining resources under applicable criteria.
choices.feedback: Correct. Individual amount and continuance evidence matters; source protection does not require ignoring a verified ending date.

choices.text: Exclude every pension payment because one component will end.
choices.feedback: An ending component does not establish that the entire pension ends or justify a categorical pension exclusion.

choices.text: Count every pension component indefinitely because retirement income is protected.
choices.feedback: Protection against automatic exclusion does not make an ending payment permanent.

choices.text: Require a younger relative to become the borrower before reviewing the records.
choices.feedback: That substitutes age and family assumptions for the individual repayment analysis.

items.prompt: A reviewer wants to understand an applicant’s stated income and actual obligations. Which inquiry is prohibited by Regulation B section 1002.5(d)(3)?

choices.text: What dependent-related financial obligations should we include, asked without a prohibited-basis distinction?
choices.feedback: The rule distinguishes appropriately neutral questions about dependents and related obligations from prohibited family-planning questions.

choices.text: What income do you want considered, with the required support-income disclosure where applicable?
choices.feedback: This can address repayment resources without compelling disclosure of support income the applicant does not want considered.

choices.text: Do you intend to have or raise children before the mortgage is repaid?
choices.feedback: Correct. Intentions concerning bearing or rearing children are prohibited inquiries, not a substitute for financial evidence.

choices.text: What current support payments are you obligated to make?
choices.feedback: Obligations to pay support are different from an inquiry about childbearing intentions.

items.prompt: Two applicants have the same product eligibility. One statement contains an unresolved transfer that requires sourcing under a lawful policy applied to all applicants; the other has no such transfer. Which response is most defensible?

choices.text: Request proportionate source evidence for the transfer and document the actual reason.
choices.feedback: Correct. Relevant individual evidence can justify a different request; consistency does not require ignoring a real difference.

choices.text: Request extra documents from both, even if they have no relevance to the other file.
choices.feedback: Identical burden is not the goal. A request should have a legitimate purpose tied to the actual file.

choices.text: Waive the sourcing requirement because any different request is discrimination.
choices.feedback: A supported nondiscriminatory difference can warrant a proportionate inquiry.

choices.text: Record national origin as the explanation because it helps identify transfer risk.
choices.feedback: National origin is not the actual sourcing discrepancy and cannot replace the relevant evidence.

items.prompt: Authorized verification confirms June salary of $5,900 monthly and a conditional increase to $6,700 beginning September. A replacement June record shows $6,700. Which file note is accurate without deciding future-income eligibility?

choices.text: June salary is verified at $6,700 because the employer confirmed that amount for September.
choices.feedback: A prospective amount does not correct the historical June record.

choices.text: Both documents are verified because each amount appears in an employer communication.
choices.feedback: The periods and conditions differ; the replacement June statement remains inconsistent with verified June pay.

choices.text: June salary is $5,900; the conditional September increase needs separate underwriting review.
choices.feedback: Correct. This preserves the verified historical fact and routes the prospective amount without converting it into past earnings.

choices.text: June salary is $5,900, so the applicant deliberately forged the replacement.
choices.feedback: The verification resolves the amount, not necessarily who created the replacement or their intent.

items.prompt: A borrower states an intention to occupy Unit A of a duplex. A current lease covers only Unit B. Which initial conclusion is best?

choices.text: The lease proves the entire property must be classified as an investment.
choices.feedback: The lease is for another unit. Read the actual intended use and applicable program rules before classifying the property.

choices.text: The occupancy statement is fully verified solely because Unit A is not in the lease.
choices.feedback: Absence from this lease does not complete every occupancy or program requirement.

choices.text: The originator should remove the lease to prevent confusion during underwriting.
choices.feedback: Removing relevant evidence hides rather than resolves the property-use question.

choices.text: The facts can coexist; verify the intended use and applicable occupancy requirements.
choices.feedback: Correct. A rented separate unit is not by itself a contradiction of intended occupancy in Unit A.

items.prompt: A report’s birth date and suffix differ from the applicant’s records. The source of the mismatch is unknown. What should the handoff say?

choices.text: The applicant is using another person’s identity and should be reported as a criminal.
choices.feedback: The mismatch does not establish deliberate misuse, responsibility, or a criminal finding.

choices.text: The report-to-applicant association is unresolved; use the approved identity and credit-report process.
choices.feedback: Correct. This identifies the reliance problem and routes verification without inventing a conclusion.

choices.text: The score is usable if the surname matches and the result is favorable.
choices.feedback: A matching surname does not resolve the material identifier differences.

choices.text: The report should be edited locally to match the application identifiers.
choices.feedback: Changing the report’s appearance does not establish whose history it contains.

items.prompt: For a covered principal-dwelling transaction, an appraisal may omit a bathroom. A manager proposes withholding future work unless the appraiser adds $15,000. Which response preserves a lawful factual review?

choices.text: Communicate the $15,000 requirement indirectly through the appraisal management company.
choices.feedback: Indirect pressure for a target outcome is not protected by using an intermediary.

choices.text: Ask the borrower to request the increase so the originator does not make the demand.
choices.feedback: Using another person to exert the same outcome pressure does not preserve independent judgment.

choices.text: Submit the bathroom evidence through the approved channel and request independent review without a target or threat.
choices.feedback: Correct. Appropriate additional information and error review are permitted; coercion and attempted coercion are prohibited.

choices.text: Treat the bathroom issue as proof of a reportable material professional violation.
choices.feedback: A possible factual error needs assessment; the facts supplied do not establish the separate material-failure reporting standard.

items.prompt: An employee uploads an unredacted customer bank statement to an unapproved public summarizing tool. What is the most appropriate immediate recommended response?

choices.text: Activate the approved incident process and preserve what was sent, when, and to which service.
choices.feedback: Correct. Prompt factual escalation supports containment and the applicable legal notification analysis; do not conceal the event.

choices.text: Wait until the customer reports misuse before involving the security team.
choices.feedback: Harm is not a prerequisite to identifying and responding to a possible unauthorized disclosure.

choices.text: Delete the browser history and mark the exposure resolved.
choices.feedback: Local deletion does not establish removal of data from the outside service and can conceal relevant evidence.

choices.text: Assume the privacy notice authorized the upload because the purpose was loan processing.
choices.feedback: A privacy notice is not blanket permission to use any external recipient or tool; approved sharing and security conditions matter.

items.prompt: At a covered mortgage company, a customer asks whether the company filed a SAR. The originator also needs an ordinary factual clarification about a deposit. Which response best respects the distinction?

choices.text: Confirm the SAR but withhold a copy, because only the form itself is confidential.
choices.feedback: Information revealing a SAR’s existence is also protected, subject to the governing exceptions.

choices.text: Do not disclose SAR existence; route the request and any needed factual inquiry through the approved compliance process.
choices.feedback: Correct. SAR confidentiality and legitimate handling of underlying transaction facts are distinct; use the authorized process.

choices.text: Promise that no report will be filed if the customer signs a corrected application.
choices.feedback: A reporting promise or threat is not an acceptable bargaining tool and can interfere with compliance duties.

choices.text: Stop all factual document requests because underlying facts are always confidential as SAR information.
choices.feedback: The rule distinguishes underlying facts, transactions, and documents from disclosure of the SAR or its existence.

items.prompt: An originator has hidden a likely-qualifying lower-cost option available through a regular creditor solely to obtain more creditor-paid compensation. No loan has yet been consummated. What is the best next step?

choices.text: Approve the practice because section 1026.36(e)(1) includes a consummation element.
choices.feedback: The absence of consummation does not make the conduct appropriate or remove the need to prevent consumer harm and review other obligations.

choices.text: Tell the customer the specified steering violation is complete even though no loan was obtained.
choices.feedback: The interpretation of this specific provision includes consummation; describe the current concern precisely.

choices.text: Obtain a general waiver allowing the originator to choose whichever option pays more.
choices.feedback: A waiver does not supply an accurate comparison or a consumer-interest justification for hiding the option.

choices.text: Correct the comparison now and route the compensation-driven recommendation for review.
choices.feedback: Correct. The specific violation’s consummation element is not a reason to delay correction of the harmful recommendation.

items.prompt: A title provider agrees to pay an outside broker’s conference airfare only after five covered settlement-service referrals close. The broker performs no service for the provider. Which conclusion best addresses the proposed educational exception?

choices.text: Airfare is outside RESPA because no cash is delivered to the broker.
choices.feedback: A thing of value can include payment of another person’s expenses.

choices.text: Calling the conference educational establishes the exception.
choices.feedback: The label does not satisfy the conditions governing promotional and educational activities.

choices.text: A signed borrower disclosure removes both concerns with the arrangement.
choices.feedback: Disclosure does not eliminate a referral condition or payment of otherwise-incurred expenses under this exception.

choices.text: The referral condition and payment of the broker’s otherwise-incurred expense defeat that exception.
choices.feedback: Correct. Section 1024.14(g)(1)(vi) has both conditions; the stated arrangement fails them.

items.prompt: An illustration has $1,760 P&I, $340 estimated monthly taxes, $115 estimated homeowners insurance, $90 mortgage insurance, and $80 association dues paid separately. The first four are collected together. What should the explanation show?

choices.text: $2,215 total outlay; taxes and homeowners insurance complete the housing cost.
choices.feedback: That sum includes P&I, taxes, and homeowners insurance but omits the $90 mortgage insurance and $80 association charge.

choices.text: $2,385 total outlay, including a $2,305 collection and $80 separate dues.
choices.feedback: Correct. $1,760 + $340 + $115 + $90 = $2,305; adding $80 gives $2,385. Identify estimates and possible changes.

choices.text: $2,305 total outlay, with the $80 already included in the collection.
choices.feedback: The stated first-four-item collection is $2,305, and the separate $80 must still be added.

choices.text: $1,760 total outlay because a fixed rate fixes every monthly housing cost.
choices.feedback: P&I is only one component; a fixed rate does not make taxes, insurance, or dues disappear or remain unchanged.

items.prompt: An ordinary covered first-lien dwelling-loan webpage advertises a payment that excludes taxes and insurance. Which proposed correction is the strongest?

choices.text: Leave the payment headline unchanged and rely on the later Closing Disclosure to explain exclusions.
choices.feedback: Later transaction disclosures do not replace applicable advertising disclosures at the advertising stage.

choices.text: Add an accurate tax-and-insurance statement anywhere on the website.
choices.feedback: The applicable rule requires prominence and close proximity, not merely existence somewhere on the site.

choices.text: Identify the exclusion and greater obligation prominently nearby, then review payment periods and all other triggered terms.
choices.feedback: Correct. This addresses the isolated defect while recognizing that the complete advertisement still needs review.

choices.text: Replace the amount with an estimated total and declare compliance without reviewing any other term.
choices.feedback: Correcting one number does not establish that all scope, payment, APR, or triggered disclosure requirements are met.

items.prompt: A customer can afford a loan only if a future refinance lowers the payment. The originator has no evidence that such a refinance will be available. What is the most responsible explanation?

choices.text: Explain today’s obligations and risks, avoid guaranteeing refinancing, and review available alternatives under accurate assumptions.
choices.feedback: Correct. A later refinance depends on future facts; it cannot be promised as the solution to today’s payment risk.

choices.text: Promise a refinance after twelve payments because payment history always guarantees approval.
choices.feedback: No such guarantee follows from the facts; future eligibility, rates, value, and other conditions can differ.

choices.text: Keep the promise if the customer signs that future rates are uncertain.
choices.feedback: A generic acknowledgment does not cure an unsupported guarantee or contradictory explanation.

choices.text: Recommend signing immediately so the consumer cannot lose the projected refinance benefit.
choices.feedback: The supposed benefit and urgency are unsupported; pressure does not create reliable evidence.
